Rohini Courts, Delhi [hereinafter referred to as "Impugned Award"].

sentences.text: By the Impugned Award, the compensation in the sum of Rs. 10,31,091/- along with 9% interest per annum has been granted to the Respondent No.1/Claimant.
2. Learned Counsel for the Appellant submits that the challenge in the present Appeal is on two grounds.
Firstly, that Respondent No. 2 [Driver] did not have a valid driving license i.e. "transport license".
The second ground of challenge is to the grant of loss of future income by the use of multiplier method.
He submits that the learned Tribunal has erred in using the multiplier method.
2.1 Learned Counsel for the Appellant submits that the learned Tribunal has relied on the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in Jagdish v. Mohan; (2018) 4 SCC 571 for the Impugned Award.
It is contended that the judgment is not applicable in the facts of the present case as the judgment

3. So far as concerns the aspect of non-grant of transport license, the learned Tribunal had dealt with this in paragraphs 18 and 19 of the Impugned Award.

It is apposite to set out the same below:
"18.
Ld. Counsel for R3/insurance company have taken the defence that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having transport license at the relevant time.

sentences.text: non-transport driving license or not.
No evidence has been placed on record by the respondents to correlate the cause of accident due to not having "Transport License".
Even otherwise, the driver of the offending vehicle was plying the vehicle as commercial or not.
In these circumstances, this point of insurance company is not valid.

19. In view of the above discussion, this tribunal is of considered opinion that R-1 is guilty of rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle at the relevant time leading to the accident in which petitioner sustained grievous injuries."
[Emphasis supplied] 3.1

On the other ground that has been taken by the learned Counsel for the Appellant, the learned Tribunal has found that paragraph 8 of the Jagdish case states that in assessing compensation, a victim who suffers a permanent or temporary disability occasioned by an accident is entitled to the award of compensation.
4. A Coordinate Bench of this Court on 18.11.2024 had directed an unconditional stay in the matter.

In view of the hearings held on 07.07.2025 and today, this Court deems it apposite to direct that the entire decretal amount inclusive of up-to-date interest shall be deposited by the Appellant within a period of 6 weeks from today.
4.1 Upon deposit, 60% of the deposited amount inclusive of up-to-date interest shall be released to the Respondent No. 1/Claimant in accordance with scheme, as is set out in the Impugned Award.

6.1 All judgments sought to be relied upon shall be filed with an index which also sets out the relevant paragraph numbers and the proposition of law that it sets forth.
The parties will act based on the digitally signed copy of the order.
